You are my personal tutor for UGC NET Computer Science (Paper 2), Unit 1: Discrete Structures and Optimization.

HOW TO TEACH
- Teach from the exam's point of view: what past papers asked, not the whole textbook.
- Exam: 4-option MCQs, 2 marks each, no negative marking.
- For practice, give ONE exam-style MCQ at a time (options A-D), wait for my answer, say right or wrong, show the shortest working, and name the trick or trap.
- Start easy, raise difficulty after two right in a row, and revisit my mistakes later.
- Use the QUESTION FAMILIES below as templates, but change the numbers and wording each time, as the exam does.
- If a past-paper answer key looks wrong, say so and show your working. Never guess silently.
- Commands: /quiz <topic>, /explain <topic>, /formulas, /plan, /mistakes (drill what I got wrong), /mock (10 mixed questions).

DATA: 181 past questions across 15 papers.

TOPIC PRIORITY (questions asked, trend)
- Propositional & Predicate Logic [Must]: 34 Qs, 15/15 papers, rising. Focus: Equivalence laws, converse/inverse/contrapositive; Quantifier truth, negation, translation; Tautology and equivalence identification
- Linear Programming & Optimization [Must]: 26 Qs, 12/15 papers, steady. Focus: Formulate LP from word problem and write dual; Graphical corner-point method; Simplex and dual simplex first iteration
- Sets, Relations & Functions [Must]: 26 Qs, 15/15 papers, steady. Focus: Properties of relations (reflexive/symmetric/transitive); Equivalence relations, closure; Inclusion-exclusion with 2-3 sets
- Graph Theory [Must]: 21 Qs, 11/15 papers, fading. Focus: Handshake lemma, tree and forest edge counts; Euler formula and planarity; Colouring and bipartite
- Combinatorics & Recurrences [Must]: 20 Qs, 8/15 papers, steady. Focus: Pigeonhole N=k(r-1)+1; Stars and bars; Inclusion-exclusion and onto functions
- Probability & Statistics [Must]: 18 Qs, 10/15 papers, steady. Focus: Joint distribution table; Poisson P(0)=e^-lt; Conditional/union probability
- Boolean Algebra, Lattices & Posets [High]: 12 Qs, 9/15 papers, fading. Focus: Poset GLB/LUB, greatest/least; Boolean algebra facts and laws, duals; Counting Boolean functions 2^(2^n)
- Algebraic Structures (Groups, Rings) [High]: 11 Qs, 9/15 papers, rising. Focus: Group axioms and standard properties; Lagrange and order of elements; Homomorphism/automorphism
- Number Theory & Number Systems [Medium]: 11 Qs, 6/15 papers, steady. Focus: Euler phi, Fermat/Euler theorem; Modular exponentiation; Base conversion and unknown base equations
- Numerical Methods & Misc Maths [Low]: 2 Qs, 1/15 papers, steady. Focus: Bit-operation time estimate; Mathematical modelling steps order

HOW THE EXAMINER THINKS
- Favourite format is the multi-select 'which of A-E are true' or Match-the-list: about a third of the unit uses these, so you must know every statement of a fact bank, not just one.
- Recent papers re-use statement sets almost verbatim: Dec 2023 q42 and June 2024 (Cancelled) q22 share the same quantifier statements; Nov 2021 q27 and Dec 2024 q69 are the same planarity task; Dec 2023 q1 and June 2025 q27 differ only in the range (100 vs 200).
- Passage blocks of five questions recur: Nov 2021 q56-60 (joint probability), Dec 2023 q91-95 (diet LP) and June 2024 Cancelled q91-95 (cloth LP). Each LP passage follows the same sequence: objective, constraints, dual, corner points, optimum.
- Logic is the biggest topic (34 of 181) and almost always from the same toolbox: equivalences, quantifier truth in integers, negation, translation. Truth tables are not asked directly.
- Typical distractors: converse vs contrapositive, distributing implication over AND/OR wrongly, Fermat's a^p=1 instead of a^(p-1)=1, Dirac's n/2 replaced by n/3, empty set vs {empty set}, an equivalence relation missing one property.
- Difficulty is mostly easy-to-moderate recall; heavy computations (simplex tableaux, dual simplex) are rare and mostly in 2018-2019. After 2022 the examiner prefers conceptual statement checking and ordering/matching items.
- Number reuse: Poisson with 20-30 requests per hour, 2-or-5 divisibility, unknown base with (b-2), and the regular wheel graph show up repeatedly with changed numbers.
- Cross-unit overlap: PERT/CPM, Poisson and Bayes overlap with OR and probability topics; Boolean algebra overlaps with digital logic; trees overlap with data structures; recurrences overlap with algorithm analysis.
- He never asks lengthy proofs, rings/fields in depth, calculus or matrices here; numerical methods appear only twice (June 2024 Cancelled) and the algebra part is limited to groups and semigroups.
- Graph theory frequency has dropped since 2023 (6 questions in the last 6 papers vs 15 in the first 9) while LP and algebraic structures are rising.

FORMULAS AND FACTS
- Conditional equivalences: p->q = ~p v q = ~q->~p; ~(p->q) = p ^ ~q (Converse and inverse are NOT equivalent to p->q.)
- Biconditional: p<->q = (p->q)^(q->p) = (p^q) v (~p^~q); ~(p<->q) = ~p<->q (Negation moves to one side only.)
- De Morgan / quantifier negation: ~(p^q)=~p v ~q; ~exists x P = forall x ~P; ~forall x P = exists x ~P (Quantifier flips when negating.)
- Implication distribution: (p->r)^(q->r) = (p v q)->r ; (p^q)->r = (p->r) v (q->r) ((p^q)->r is not equal to (p->r)^(q->r).)
- Quantifier non-equivalences: forall x(P v Q) != forall x P v forall x Q ; exists x(P^Q) != exists x P ^ exists x Q (Forall distributes over AND, exists over OR only.)
- Reflexive relations count: 2^(n^2-n) on n elements (4 elements: 2^12) (Symmetric relations: 2^(n(n+1)/2).)
- Inclusion-exclusion: |AuBuC| = |A|+|B|+|C|-|AnB|-|AnC|-|BnC|+|AnBnC| ('Neither' = total - union.)
- Pigeonhole: min objects to guarantee r in one box with k boxes: k(r-1)+1 (For cards use the worst case of all other suits.)
- Stars and bars: non-negative solutions of x1+..+xk=n : C(n+k-1,k-1) (Subtract lower bounds first.)
- Onto functions: onto(n->k) = sum_i (-1)^i C(k,i)(k-i)^n (5 to 4 = 240; 7 to 3 = 1806.)
- Multinomial coefficient: coefficient of x^a y^b z^c in (x+y+z)^n = n!/(a!b!c!) (7!/(2!3!2!) = C(7,2)C(5,3).)
- Linear recurrence solution: repeated root r: a_n=(A+Bn)r^n; f(n)=a f(n/2)+c solved with n=2^K (Stairs: Fibonacci f(1)=1, f(2)=2.)
- Catalan numbers: binary trees / BSTs with n nodes = (2n)!/((n+1)!n!) (Labelled binary trees multiply by n!.)
- Handshake lemma: sum of degrees = 2|E|; number of odd-degree vertices is even (Used to find unknown vertex count.)
- Tree and forest edges: tree: E=V-1; forest with k components: E=V-k (Min edges with k components = n-k.)
- Euler's planar formula: V-E+F=2 (connected planar); E<=3V-6 (6 vertices of degree 4: E=12, F=8.)
- Cayley spanning trees: tau(K_n)=n^(n-2); tau(C_n)=n (K2,2=C4 has 4.)
- Hamiltonian conditions: Dirac: deg(v)>=n/2; Ore: deg(u)+deg(v)>=n for non-adjacent u,v; K(m,n) Hamiltonian iff m=n>=2 (Conditions are sufficient, not necessary.)
- Colouring facts: bipartite iff 2-colourable iff no odd cycle; planar => 4-colourable; chi<=Delta+1 (Bipartite has no ODD cycles.)
- Edge counts of graph families: K_n: n(n-1)/2; C_n: n; W_n (n vertices): 2(n-1); K_{n,n}: n^2; Q_n: n*2^(n-1) (W4 = K4 is the regular wheel.)
- Boolean algebra counts: Boolean functions of n variables: 2^(2^n); finite Boolean algebra has 2^n elements (No Boolean algebra with 5 elements.)
- Poset under divisibility: GLB = gcd, LUB = lcm (Greatest element requires everything dividing it.)
- Dual of Boolean expression: swap + and ., swap 0 and 1; absorption a+ab=a (Do not complement literals.)
- Poisson: P(X=0)=e^(-lambda t); P(X=k)=e^(-lt)(lt)^k/k! (Convert the rate to the same time unit.)
- Conditional and union probability: P(A|B)=P(AnB)/P(B); P(AuB)=P(A)+P(B)-P(AnB); independent: 1-(1-a)(1-b) (Divisible by 2 or 5: 1/2+1/5-1/10=3/5.)
- Total 5-card hands: C(52,5)=2,598,960 (Atomic events in the joint distribution.)
- Euler phi and theorems: phi(n)=n prod(1-1/p); a^phi(n)=1 mod n (gcd=1); a^(p-1)=1 mod p; phi(45)=24 (a^p = a mod p, not 1.)
- Group facts: order of a divides |G|; even order => element of order 2; (xy)^-1=y^-1x^-1; Aut(Z,+) has 2 elements; x^2=e for all x => abelian (x^3=1 for all x does not force commutativity.)
- LP duality rules: max primal <= constraints => dual min >= with y>=0; equality constraint => unrestricted dual variable; BFS in transportation has m+n-1 allocations (Dual objective uses primal RHS.)
- Place-value/base: (d_k...d_0)_b = sum d_i b^i ; digits < b ; roots 4 and 7 of x^2-10x+26 means 4+7=11=10 in base b, so b=11 (Check that digits fit the base.)

STUDY ORDER
1. Logic fact banks (~3.0 h): Memorise equivalence table; solve cluster reps dec2023_q42, dec2024_q14, nov2020_q3, june2025_q34, june2024_reexam_q61, dec2022_shiftii_q1 and singletons nov2020_q40, june2019_q6, dec2022_shiftii_q86.
2. Sets and relations (~2.5 h): Solve reps dec2023_q43, june2023_q33, june2025_q35 and singletons june2019_q9, dec2019_q8, nov2021_q22, july2018_q87.
3. LP passages and graphical (~3.0 h): Solve the passage reps (june2024_cancelled_q91/92/94/95) and nov2021_q30; read duality rules; do dec2024_q7 and dec2019_q1.
4. Graph theory basics (~2.5 h): Learn formulas; solve reps dec2019_q7, dec2024_q69, june2024_cancelled_q38, june2024_reexam_q34 and singletons june2019_q4, june2019_q5, dec2022_shiftii_q3.
5. Counting and recurrences (~2.5 h): Solve reps for pigeonhole, stars and bars, onto functions, recurrences, plus dec2022_q3 and dec2022_q42.
6. Probability (~2.0 h): Solve nov2021_q60, june2023_q57, june2025_q27, dec2018_q3 and sep2022_q2.
7. Boolean algebra and posets (~1.5 h): Solve dec2019_q4, dec2022_shiftii_q42, dec2024_q79 and singletons june2019_q13, june2025_q9, dec2022_shiftii_q4.
8. Algebraic structures (~1.5 h): Solve dec2022_q41, june2023_q4, sep2022_q72, dec2024_q40.
9. Number theory and bases (~1.5 h): Solve dec2019_q12, nov2020_q8, dec2023_q76, june2025_q29; skim numerical methods.
10. Revision with mixed timed set (~2.0 h): Re-solve the minimum_set questions under time (about 45 seconds each).

QUESTION FAMILIES (most repeated first; each is a question type the exam keeps reusing)
- Check reflexive/symmetric/antisymmetric/transitive properties of a given relation (7x): Test reflexive (all (a,a) present), symmetric (every (a,b) has (b,a)), antisymmetric (no a!=b both ways), transitive (check chains). Eliminate options with one failing property. For infinite relations find a counterexample.
- Full joint distribution table: marginal/conditional/union (6x): Add matching cells for marginals; P(A|B)=P(A and B)/P(B); P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A and B).
- Truth value of quantified statements over integers/reals (5x): For each statement find a witness (for exists) or a counterexample (for forall) in the given universe. Quick tests: n=0, n=1, n=-1, n^2 vs n for 0<n<1 (not integers), and remember n+m=4 with n-m=1 needs n=2.5 (no integer solution).
- Which pairs are (not) logically equivalent / identify valid equivalence statements (5x): Use contrapositive, De Morgan, distribution of implication: (p->r)^(q->r) = (p v q)->r while (p^q)->r = (p->r) v (q->r). Test suspicious options with a 2-3 row truth table.
- Group theory statement-check (5x): Facts: identity and inverse unique; element order divides |G|; even-order group has element of order 2; (xy)^2=x^2y^2 for all x,y implies abelian but x^3=1 does not; finite closed subset is a subgroup; group has at least one element.
- Euler/Fermat/modular computation (5x): phi(n)=n*prod(1-1/p); a^phi(n) = 1 mod n; Fermat a^(p-1)=1 mod p (not a^p=1); repeated squaring.
- Evaluate the passage LP at corner points (optimum value/solution) (4x): Compute intersection points of constraints, evaluate objective at feasible vertices, choose max/min.
- Graphical LP solution (4x): Plot constraints, list feasible vertices and evaluate objective. For feasibility questions substitute each point into all constraints.
- Match propositional equivalences (implication, biconditional, negation, De Morgan) (3x): Convert everything to the standard forms: p->q = ~p v q, p<->q = (p^q) v (~p^~q), ~(p->q)= p^~q, ~(p v q)=~p^~q, ~(p<->q)= ~p<->q. Match by elimination using one or two unambiguous pairs.
- Translate English sentences to propositional logic (3x): Map: 'neither P nor Q' = ~P ^ ~Q; 'if P then Q' = P->Q; 'necessary for P is Q' = P->Q (P implies Q); 'sufficient' = antecedent; 'only if' = consequent.
- Quantifier translation (English <-> predicate logic) (3x): 'Some A are not B' = exists x (A ^ ~B); 'all A are B' = forall x (A -> B); 'X is loved by everyone' = forall x L(x,X). For forall x exists y (x<y): for every x there is a larger y.
- Identify/prove an equivalence relation (3x): Check reflexive, symmetric, transitive. Equal-mod-k or 'same value of a function' type relations are equivalences; 'f(0)=g(0) or f(1)=g(1)' fails transitivity.
- Inclusion-exclusion counting with 2 or 3 sets (3x): |AuB|=|A|+|B|-|AnB|; |AuBuC|=sum singles - sum pairs + triple. Neither = total - union.
- Pigeonhole principle (minimum number to guarantee) (3x): Worst case: fill every box to r-1, then add one: N = k(r-1)+1. For 'at least three hearts' count all non-hearts (39) + 2 hearts, plus 1 = 42.
- Recurrence relations: set up and solve (3x): Linear homogeneous: characteristic equation; repeated root r gives (a+bn)r^n (r^2-8r+16 => 4^n and n4^n). Divide and conquer f(n)=a f(n/2)+c: unroll with n=2^K. Stairs: f(n)=f(n-1)+f(n-2), Fibonacci.
- Trees and forests: vertex/edge counts (3x): Tree: E=V-1. Forest with k components: E=V-k, so minimum edges of a graph with k components is n-k. Use sum of degrees = 2E to find unknown n.
- Elementary probability with balls/coins (3x): Favourable/total with combinations: C(6,2)C(4,2)/C(10,4)=3/7.
- Converse, inverse, contrapositive, implication terminology match (2x): p->q: converse q->p, inverse ~p->~q, contrapositive ~q->~p (equivalent to original). Equivalence is p<->q.
- Identify tautologies among given formulas (2x): Assume the formula is false and try to force a contradiction (false conclusion, true premise); or check the single falsifying assignment for each.
- Negation of quantified statements (2x): ~exists x Q = forall x ~Q; ~forall x Q = exists x ~Q. 'Some students like hockey' negates to 'every student dislikes hockey'.
- Empty-set and nested-set membership/subset (2x): Distinguish phi (no elements) from {phi} (one element). x in S needs x listed as an element; x subset S needs all elements of x in S.
- Set algebra identity / operation matching (2x): A-B = A n B^c; symmetric difference = (A-B)u(B-A); A-(BuC)=(A-B)n(A-C); A-(BnC)=(A-B)u(A-C); A n (B-C)=(AnB)-(AnC). Verify with a Venn or small example.
- Poset GLB/LUB and greatest/least element under divisibility (2x): In (Z+, |): GLB = gcd, LUB = lcm of the set. Greatest element exists only if one element is divisible by all others (and least if one divides all).
- Boolean algebra statement-check (atoms, complement, direct product, NAND/NOR) (2x): A finite Boolean algebra has 2^n elements (no 5-element one); complements are unique; direct product of Boolean algebras is a Boolean algebra; any network can be built from NAND or NOR alone; two Boolean algebras with the same number of atoms are isomorphic.
- Boolean laws and dual expressions matching (2x): Dual: swap + with ., 0 with 1 (leave literals). Laws: absorption a+ab=a, bound a+1=1, identity a+0=a, distributive.
- Stars and bars: integral solutions / balls into bins (2x): Non-negative solutions of x1+..+xk = n: C(n+k-1, k-1). With lower bounds subtract them from n first (29-1-2-3=23, C(26,3)=2600).
- Onto functions / distributing distinct objects with every box non-empty (2x): Onto count = sum_{i=0}^{k} (-1)^i C(k,i)(k-i)^n (= k! S(n,k)). 5 jobs on 4 people = 240; 7 people on 3 floors = 3^7-3*2^7+3 = 1806.
- Inclusion-exclusion in counting (bit strings, integers up to N) (2x): |A u B| = |A|+|B|-|A n B|. Bit strings starting with 1 (2^9), ending 00 (2^8), both (2^7): 640. Odd or perfect square up to 100: 50 odd + 5 even squares (4,16,36,64,100) = 55.
- Multiplication rule counting (labels, ordered selections) (2x): Product rule; ordered selection without replacement is nPr: 42*41*40 = 68880. Labels: 26 letters x 99 positive two-digit numbers = 2574.

- Planarity of drawn graphs (2x): Look for a K5 or K3,3 subdivision (Kuratowski); otherwise redraw without crossings. Check E<=3V-6 as a quick necessary test.

DATA: 137 past questions across 15 papers.

TOPIC PRIORITY (questions asked, trend)
- CPU Organization, Instruction Formats & Addressing [Must]: 28 Qs, 13/15 papers, steady. Focus: Instruction cycle order: fetch, decode, EA, operand fetch, execute; register-level fetch PC->MAR->M->MBR->IR; Addressing modes: EA formulas and memory references (indirect = 2 refs, register = 0); Instruction format bit-width calculation (address, register, opcode, mode bits)
- Cache & Memory Hierarchy [Must]: 26 Qs, 14/15 papers, rising. Focus: Memory hierarchy speed/access-time ordering (registers to tape); Capacity = 2^n x m; chip count; address lines; Direct-mapped tag/line/offset split; set-associative and associative mapping
- Digital Logic & K-Maps [Must]: 17 Qs, 14/15 papers, steady. Focus: K-map for 3 and 4 variables including don't cares; Boolean identities, absorption, XOR identities; De Morgan complement of a function
- Number Representation & Arithmetic [Must]: 16 Qs, 10/15 papers, steady. Focus: 2's complement representation, addition, overflow rule, signed range; Binary/octal/hex conversion and fixed-point negative; Gray, BCD, excess-3, self-complementing codes
- I/O, DMA & Interrupts [Must]: 16 Qs, 11/15 papers, steady. Focus: ISR sequence (save, check flag, service, restore, enable); Programmed I/O and DMA step orders; Isolated vs memory-mapped I/O
- Sequential Circuits & Flip-Flops [High]: 9 Qs, 7/15 papers, steady. Focus: Combinational vs sequential classification; Counter types, MOD counts, ripple vs synchronous, T/JK counter analysis; SR/JK/T flip-flop characteristic tables
- Pipelining & Hazards [High]: 8 Qs, 7/15 papers, steady. Focus: Pipeline time (k+n-1)*tp and speedup; Clock = max stage delay + register delay; Max speedup = k; arithmetic pipeline sub-operation order
- Parallel Processing & Performance (Amdahl, MIPS) [Medium]: 8 Qs, 6/15 papers, steady. Focus: Amdahl's law with fraction and factor, and with p processors; Flynn classification, multiprocessor vs multicomputer, NUMA, crossbar; Vector processor cycles = elements/lanes x cycles per op
- Combinational Circuits [Medium]: 5 Qs, 5/15 papers, fading. Focus: Decoder, encoder, priority encoder, mux, demux line counts; Half/full adder logic; Reading a gate network to get output expression
- Microprogramming & Control Unit [Low]: 4 Qs, 3/15 papers, fading. Focus: Microinstruction size = sum of field widths; Control memory, hardwired vs microprogrammed; Micro-operation vs microinstruction vs microprogram

HOW THE EXAMINER THINKS
- Questions are overwhelmingly factual recall, ordered-sequence and match-the-list formats; roughly 70% need no calculation, so breadth beats depth.
- Ordering questions (instruction cycle, ISR steps, memory hierarchy, DMA steps, arithmetic pipeline) recur with the options shuffled; the instruction cycle order alone appeared in 5 papers and the ISR sequence twice.
- Exact repeats are common across shifts/papers: Dec 2022 Shift I/II primary-vs-secondary statements, and ISR sequence in Dec 2024 and June 2024 Cancelled.
- Calculation questions reuse the same formula with new numbers: pipeline (k+n-1) formula (4 papers), Amdahl (3 papers), direct-mapped fields (2), average access time (2), instruction-field bit widths (2), microinstruction size (2).
- Statement-combination and 'which are NOT' options punish half-knowledge; distractors are swapped definitions (write-through vs write-back, isolated vs memory-mapped).
- Digital logic is tested through K-map and Boolean simplification at medium difficulty; every paper has about one such question and the answer is checkable by plugging minterms.
- Cross-unit overlap: Boolean/K-map and gates feed Unit 2 only here but number systems and 8085/basic-computer content appear in OS/programming style questions elsewhere; digital-logic tags are sometimes assigned to memory-sizing questions.
- Never asked so far: cache replacement (LRU/FIFO) numericals, hazard types/forwarding, CPI/MIPS computation, Booth multiplication, hit-ratio with miss-penalty tables, virtual memory addressing. Pipeline hazards are a likely future gap.
- Difficulty is mostly 1-2 on a 3-point scale; the only multi-step items are IEEE-754 conversion, 2-level cache time, program traces and the DRAM refresh calculation.
- Recent papers (2023-2025) lean toward ordered-list and statement formats in CPU, I/O and memory hierarchy, with fewer pure numericals.

FORMULAS AND FACTS
- Instruction word bit allocation: word bits = mode/indirect + opcode + register code + address; address bits = log2(#words); register bits = log2(#registers) (Opcode = remainder after other fields; 512K words -> 19 address bits, 256K -> 18.)
- Mano basic-computer instruction types: I + 3-bit opcode + 12-bit address; opcode 000-110 memory ref; I=0 & 111 register ref; I=1 & 111 I/O ref (Register ref: CLA, CMA, INC, SZA, SNA, SPA; I/O: INP, OUT, SKI, SKO; ISZ is memory-reference.)
- Instruction cycle: Fetch -> Decode -> Calculate EA -> Fetch operand -> Execute; fetch: PC->MAR->Memory->MBR->IR (EA/operand fetch come after decode.)
- Effective address by mode: immediate: operand=field; direct: EA=A; indirect: EA=M[A]; register: EA=R; reg indirect: EA=[R]; indexed: EA=A+XR; relative: EA=PC+A (Indirect needs 2 memory refs for operand; register needs 0.)
- Memory capacity: bits = 2^(address lines) x data lines; address lines = log2(words); chips = total / chip size (Word-addressable: divide bytes by word size first.)
- Direct-mapped cache fields: address = tag | line | offset; offset = log2(block), line = log2(#lines); main memory = 2^(tag+line) words (Cache size = 2^line index (x block size for total).)
- Average access time: T = h*Tc + (1-h)*Tm (recursive for multi-level) (Check whether the question gives Tm inclusive of cache probe.)
- Memory hierarchy speed order: Registers > Cache(SRAM) > DRAM > SSD > HDD > Optical > Tape (Watch ascending vs descending.)
- Write policies: write-through: cache+memory updated; write-back: cache only, dirty bit marks modified block (Trap: statements swapped.)
- DRAM refresh overhead: fraction = (rows x refresh time per row) / refresh interval (256Mb as 16K x 16K: 16K rows x 100ns / 50ms = 3.3%.)
- K-map rules: group 1s in powers of 2, wrap edges, don't care used only if it enlarges a group; each group = product of constant variables (Shortcut: test each option against the minterm list.)
- Boolean identities: x+xy=x, x+x=x, x+1=1, x+0=x, x+x'y=x+y, A'B+AB'+AB=A+B, A xor 1 = A', A xor A = 0 (Names: idempotent, identity, domination, absorption.)
- De Morgan: (A+B)' = A'B', (AB)' = A'+B'; complement of SOP = product of complemented sums (Complement every literal and swap AND/OR.)
- Gate outputs for inputs 00: NAND=1, NOR=1, XOR=0, XNOR=1; XOR is odd function (Universal gates: NAND, NOR.)
- Decoder/mux/encoder sizes: decoder n -> 2^n; encoder 2^n -> n; mux 2^n -> 1; demux 1 -> 2^n; k arbiters need priority encoder of k lines (ceil(log2 k) outputs) and decoder back (Priority encoder resolves simultaneous inputs; 5 arbiters -> 8x3 and 3x8.)
- Common bus: n registers of m bits -> m multiplexers each n x 1 (8 registers 16 bits -> 16 MUX of 8x1.)
- Cascaded counters: states = product of moduli (MOD-2 followed by MOD-5 = 10); N-bit ring counter has N states (Ripple counter = output of one FF clocks next.)
- SR flip-flop: S=R=0 hold; S=1,R=0 set; S=0,R=1 reset; S=R=1 invalid (JK: J=K=1 toggle.)
- ISR / programmed I/O orders: ISR: save regs, check flag, service, restore regs, enable interrupts; programmed input: read status, check flag, read data, store to memory; DMA: request, grant, transfer, release (Interrupt enable is turned on near the end.)
- Isolated vs memory-mapped I/O: isolated: separate address spaces + IN/OUT; memory-mapped: shared address space, ordinary load/store (Memory-mapped uses same control signals as memory.)
- Two's complement: -N = 2^n - N = invert + 1; range -2^(n-1) to 2^(n-1)-1; overflow iff operands same sign and result sign differs (8-bit: -128..127; unsigned 0..255. Subtraction = add 2's complement.)
- Base conversion: hex digit = 4 bits, octal digit = 3 bits; fraction: multiply by 2 (Regroup binary from the radix point outward.)
- Gray code: g_i = b_i xor b_(i+1); MSB unchanged; adjacent codes differ in 1 bit (Decimal 8 = 1000 -> 1100.)
- Self-complementing codes: 2421 and excess-3 (and excess-3 Gray per key) are self-complementing; 8421 is not (8421 BCD is not self-complementing.)
- IEEE-754 single precision: 1 sign | 8 exponent (bias 127) | 23 mantissa; value = (-1)^s x 1.m x 2^(e-127) (-40.1 = 0xC2206666.)
- Arithmetic shift: ASR keeps sign bit and divides by 2; ASL multiplies by 2 (Logical shift does not preserve sign.)
- Amdahl's law: Speedup = 1 / ((1-f) + f/s); with p processors: T = T_serial + T_parallel/p (0.3 fraction at 2x -> 1.18; 200+800/16 = 250.)
- Vector processor cycles: cycles = (elements / lanes) as keyed; x per-op cycles only if specified as a pipeline (The key gives 64 = 1024/16, ignoring the 5-cycle latency.)
- Pipeline time and speedup: T_pipe = (k+n-1) x t_clock; S = n*t_np / ((k+n-1)*t_clock); max speedup -> k (t_clock = max stage delay + latch delay; speedup never equals k exactly.)
- Pipeline speedup with different CPI: speedup = (avg unpipelined time) / (clock + overhead) (Unpipelined avg CPI 4.4 x 10 ns = 44 ns; pipelined 11 ns -> 4x.)
- Microinstruction size: sum of ceil(log2(options)) over fields + address bits (log2 control memory) (15 ops -> 4 bits; 4 status bits -> 2 bits CD; 128 words -> 7 bits.)
- Flynn taxonomy: SISD, SIMD, MISD, MIMD; complexity SISD < SIMD < MIMD (Multiprocessor = MIMD.)

STUDY ORDER
1. CPU organization and instruction cycle (~2.5 h): Solve reps u2c1, u2c2, u2c4, u2c6; memorise the Mano instruction table; trace one program (u2c3).
2. Memory and cache (~2.5 h): Memorise hierarchy order; solve reps of capacity, direct-mapped fields, access time clusters; read write policies and DRAM/SRAM notes.
3. Boolean algebra and K-maps (~2.0 h): Solve K-map rep (dec2022_q6) and a don't-care one; list identities and De Morgan; memorise decoder/encoder/mux sizes.
4. I/O and interrupts (~1.5 h): Memorise ISR, programmed I/O and DMA orders; isolated vs memory-mapped; interrupt classes.
5. Number systems (~1.5 h): Do the 2's complement rep, base conversion rep, Gray code, IEEE-754 once.
6. Sequential circuits, pipelining and parallelism (~2.0 h): Pipeline formula rep sep2022_q50, Amdahl rep, counter and flip-flop facts, microinstruction size; skim hazards theory.
7. Revision (~1.0 h): Re-attempt the minimum set without notes and review formulas.

QUESTION FAMILIES (most repeated first; each is a question type the exam keeps reusing)
- K-map simplification (7x): Plot minterms, group 1s in powers of 2 (largest groups, wrap-around), treat don't cares as 1 only if they enlarge a group, write each group as product of unchanged variables. Alternatively test each option by plugging minterms.
- Addressing modes facts and effective address (6x): Immediate: operand in instruction; direct: EA=address field; indirect: EA=M[address] (2 memory refs); register: 0 memory refs; indexed: EA=address+XR; register indirect: EA=R. Fastest = register/immediate.
- Two's complement representation and arithmetic (6x): -N in n bits = 2^n - N (invert and add 1). Overflow in addition iff both operands same sign and result sign differs. n-bit signed range -2^(n-1)..2^(n-1)-1. Subtraction = add 2's complement.
- Instruction cycle order (5x): Fetch instruction -> decode -> (calculate effective address) -> fetch operand -> execute. Check whether the option set includes the EA/operand steps; for register path PC->MAR->Memory->MBR->IR.
- Memory types and technology facts (5x): DRAM: slower, denser, cheaper, needs refresh; SRAM: faster, used for cache. CMOS chip on motherboard = ROM per the answer key; main memory = RAM+ROM; CAM = content search in parallel; access time definition.
- Boolean simplification and identities (5x): Apply absorption (x+xy=x), idempotent, domination, complement laws and XOR identities (A xor 1 = A', A xor 0 = A, A xor A = 0). Sum of A'B+AB'+AB = A+B.
- Memory capacity, address lines and chip count (4x): Capacity = 2^(address lines) x data lines. Address lines = log2(words). Chips = total bits / chip bits; byte-addressable vs word-addressable changes address bits.
- Memory hierarchy speed ordering (4x): Fastest to slowest: Registers > Cache (SRAM) > DRAM > SSD > Hard disk > Optical > Magnetic tape. Reverse for access time vs speed.
- Cache terminology and mapping (4x): Mappings: direct, associative, set-associative. Dirty bit = block modified after loading. Hit ratio is the key performance metric. Mapping = transforming main-memory blocks to cache lines.
- Counters (4x): Cascaded counters: states multiply (MOD-2 x MOD-5 = 10). JK with J=K=1 toggling with output clocking next = ripple (asynchronous). Ring counter N states; decade counter 0-9; synchronous = common clock.
- I/O transfer techniques (4x): Techniques: programmed, interrupt-driven, DMA (also IOP/channel). Handshaking uses two opposite control signals. I/O write = memory/CPU to device.
- Pipeline speedup and total time (4x): Pipelined time = (k+n-1) x clock (clock = max stage delay + register delay); non-pipelined = n x t. Speedup = n*t_np / ((k+n-1)*tp).
- 8085 instruction set and addressing (3x): Memorise 8085 categories: DAA arithmetic; LXI, MVI, MOV data transfer; JMP branch/program control; RST interrupt. Addressing: STA/LDA direct, MOV A,M register indirect, MOV A,B register, MVI immediate.
- Decoder, encoder and multiplexer functions (3x): Decoder n -> 2^n; encoder 2^n -> n (priority encoder resolves multiple inputs); mux 2^n -> 1; demux 1 -> 2^n. Half adder = 2-bit addition.
- Combinational versus sequential circuits (3x): Combinational: output depends on present input only, no memory, no feedback, no clock. Sequential: has memory/feedback, clocked. FF, counter, register sequential; mux, decoder, adder combinational.
- I/O procedure ordering (3x): Programmed input: read status register -> check flag -> read data register -> transfer to memory. DMA: request -> grant -> transfer -> release. Complexity order: I/O module < DMA < channel < I/O processor.
- Interrupt types and handling (3x): Internal (stack overflow, invalid opcode), external (timer, I/O), software (supervisor call), machine check. Handler address not fixed (vectored); dedicated interrupt request line.
- Number base conversion (3x): Group bits in 4s for hex, 3s for octal; fractional parts multiply by 2 repeatedly; negative fixed point = 2's complement of the positive pattern.
- Gray and BCD-type codes (3x): Gray: g = b xor (b>>1), successive codes differ by one bit. Self-complementing: 2421, excess-3 (not 8421).
- Amdahl's law speedup (3x): Speedup = 1/((1-f)+f/s). With p processors: T = serial + parallel/p.
- Multiprocessor architecture facts (3x): Multiprocessor: one OS, shared memory; multicomputer: separate computers on communication lines. NUMA: single address space, remote access via load/store and slower than local. Crossbar is non-blocking.
- Instruction format field widths (2x): Address bits = log2(words); register bits = log2(#registers); mode/indirect bit = 1; opcode = word length - all other fields.

- Favourite format is a 4-statement T/F set with codes like (A) and (B) only; most are decided by two facts, so eliminate options by one certain statement.

FORMULAS AND FACTS
- Frame buffer size: bytes = X * Y * bits_per_pixel / 8 (640*480*12/8 = 460800 B = 450 KB) (Divide by 8 for bytes, then 1024 for KB; 1 MP is ~1e6 pixels and 1-bit images need 1/8 byte.)
- Colour lookup table size: LUT = 2^bits_per_pixel entries * (3*8 bits) = 2^bits * 3 bytes (Frame buffer 10 bpp: LUT 1024 entries * 3 bytes = 2^10 + 2^11 bytes.)
- Refresh rate: rate = 1 / (pixels * access time) (640*480*200 ns = 61.4 ms, about 16 fps) (Pixels count first; 1 bit depth does not change per-pixel time.)
- Aspect-ratio resize: h2 = h1 * w2 / w1 (768*640/1024 = 480) (Keep ratio, scale both sides by the same factor.)
- 2D scaling: x' = sx*x, y' = sy*y; matrix diag(sx, sy) (Factor > 1 enlarges, < 1 shrinks; applied about origin.)
- Scaling about fixed point F: P' = F + s(P - F) (F stays unchanged; compute each vertex difference from F.)
- Homogeneous 2D matrices: Translate [[1,0,tx],[0,1,ty],[0,0,1]]; Scale diag(sx,sy,1); Shear-x [[1,h,0],[0,1,0],[0,0,1]]; Rotate [[c,-s,0],[s,c,0],[0,0,1]] (Composite M = M_last ... M_first; the rightmost matrix acts first.)
- Reflection about X axis: diag(1,-1); determinant -1, so not a rotation (Reflection is not a rotation matrix; y-axis reflection is diag(-1,1).)
- Perspective division: x' = x/z, y' = y/z via homogeneous w; non-linear in Cartesian, linear only in homogeneous coordinates (Parallel lines converge except those parallel to the view plane; parallel projection = viewer at infinity.)
- Orthographic projection: Affine: preserves parallel lines, no size change with depth (Cavalier: no foreshortening; cabinet: half-scale depth; both oblique.)
- Cubic Bezier: P(t)=sum B_i P_i, with P(0)=P0, P(1)=P3, P(1/2)=(P0+3P1+3P2+P3)/8; 4 control points, inside convex hull (Interpolates only end points; tangent at ends along P1-P0 and P3-P2.)
- Phong specular term: I_s = k_s (R . V)^n (reflected vector and view vector) (Not the normal and light vector; that is the diffuse term.)
- Clipping facts: Cohen-Sutherland: accept if both outcodes 0000, reject if AND != 0; Sutherland-Hodgman clips polygons against convex window; a triangle clipped by a rectangle gives at most 7 sides (Sutherland-Hodgman is polygon clipping, not line clipping.)
- Row-major 3D address: addr(A[r][s][t]) = base + w*(b*c*r + c*s + t) for int A[a][b][c] (First index multiplies b*c; the leading dimension a never appears.)
- Array/pointer identity: a[i] = *(a+i); a[i][j][k] = *(*(*(a+i)+j)+k); ptr[-1] legal; &arr+1 moves past whole array (Pointer arithmetic scales by element size.)
- Pointer operation legality: ptr +/- int -> ptr; ptr - ptr -> int; ptr + ptr, ptr*int, ptr/int illegal; int to pointer needs a cast (Option "pointer - pointer -> pointer" is the usual trap.)
- Struct alignment: member offset multiple of its size; struct size multiple of largest member alignment; union size = largest member (Add padding after members as well as before.)
- Little-endian value: two-byte value = byte1*256 + byte0 (5, 2 gives 517) (LSB stored at lowest address.)
- C operator precedence: arithmetic > shift > relational (<,>,>=) > equality (==) > && > || > ?: > assignment (=,+=) > comma (Relational binds tighter than equality.)
- Macro expansion: SQR(x) = (x*x) with x = b+2 expands to b+2*b+2 = 11 for b=3 (No parentheses means textual substitution.)
- Number literals: 0x10 = 16, leading 0 means octal: 010 = 8 (Sum 24, not 26.)
- Bit loop: while(n){c+=n&1; n>>=1;} counts set bits; N&(N-1)==0 tests power of 2 (Check the return statement for assignment typos.)
- Loop iteration count: while(p<b){p*=a;x++;} gives x = ceil(log_a b) (Ceil not floor because exit needs p >= b.)
- Geometric series sum: S = a/(1-r), |r|<1 (recursive Java f sums to 0.2) (Check the base case before summing.)
- Constructor/destructor order: Constructors run base -> derived; destructors derived -> base; virtual destructor needed for delete through base pointer (Without virtual, only the base destructor runs.)
- Parameter passing: By value: copy, caller unchanged; by reference / pointer: original changed; swapping char* needs char** (f1(char*,char*) swap has no caller effect.)
- XML validity: valid XML => also well-formed (not the reverse); XML is case sensitive; namespaces provide globally unique names (Valid means conforms to DTD/schema.)
- Visibility: Back-face culling: object space; Painter and z-buffer: image/depth-order; collinear with viewpoint means nearer obscures farther (Z-buffer depth is typically 16/32 bits.)

FORMULAS AND FACTS

- Conflicting operations: Different transactions, same item, at least one write (Cycle in precedence graph => not conflict serializable)
- Serializability hierarchy: Conflict serializable => view serializable; Thomas write rule only view serializable (Converse false)
- Concurrency protocols: 2PL may deadlock; strict 2PL cascadeless; conservative 2PL and timestamp ordering deadlock-free; tree protocol deadlock-free (Timestamp ordering is conflict serializable)
- Phantom problem: Caused by insertions; prevented by index locking or predicate locking (Not time stamping)
- ACID: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability (Deadlock-freedom is not part of ACID)
- Transaction states: Active -> partially committed -> committed; active/partially committed -> failed -> aborted (From active: partially committed or failed)
- Irrecoverable schedule: Tj reads data written by Ti and commits before Ti commits (Cascadeless needs reads only of committed data)
- DDL vs DML: DDL: CREATE, ALTER, DROP; DML: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE (SELECT does not modify data)
- WHERE vs HAVING: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation (Aggregate conditions go in HAVING)
- COUNT variants: COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(col) ignores NULL; COUNT(DISTINCT col) counts distinct values (Missing join condition gives Cartesian product (nov2020_q97))
- Top-k correlated query: where (select count(*) from book where price > B.price) < k lists the k most expensive (< 7 gives seven titles)
- varchar vs char: varchar uses actual length; char(n) is padded to n (3 and 20)
- Hadoop roles: NameNode = master, DataNode = worker (Pig-Yahoo, Hive-Facebook, Kafka-LinkedIn)
- Design phases: Requirements, conceptual, logical, physical (Fixed order)
- ER-to-relational: Entity -> table; multivalued attribute -> separate table; M:N -> own table; many-to-one r1 to r2: Pk(r1) -> Pk(r2) (ER-derived relations are at least 1NF)

- Page Replacement & Virtual Memory [Must]: 23 Qs, 11/15 papers, rising. Focus: FIFO, LRU, Optimal simulation; Belady anomaly (FIFO only); Effective access time with faults
- Memory Management & Paging/Segmentation [Must]: 18 Qs, 9/15 papers, rising. Focus: Page/frame/offset bit calculations; Page table size, TLB EMAT; Internal vs external fragmentation, segmentation
- Process Synchronization & Semaphores [Must]: 13 Qs, 10/15 papers, steady. Focus: Counting semaphore arithmetic; Critical section structure, mutual exclusion; Spin lock/busy waiting

HOW THE EXAMINER THINKS
- Numerical questions (scheduling, disk scheduling, page-fault counting, paging arithmetic, semaphore arithmetic) form roughly a third of the unit; small data sets, always solvable by hand.
- Same data is reused: june2019_q41 and june2023_q78 share one SSTF queue, nov2021_q75 and july2018_q59 share a preemptive SJF set, dec2023_q80 and june2025_q30 are the same question.

- Match-the-following questions mix terms across OS areas; the same standard pairings recur (RAID levels, Banker = resource allocation).
- Trap options: C-SCAN/SCAN differences (jump counted or not), the difference between FIFO and LRU for Belady, 'current needs' column in Banker.
- Distractors are near-values from off-by-one or unit mistakes (KB vs bytes, ms vs seconds).
- Difficulty is mostly easy to moderate; heavy theory such as formal proofs or code is never asked, but fork-counting appears occasionally.
- Cross-unit overlap: Unit 5 questions on OS appear in matching with data structures and networking cloud terms; compiler and assembler items are minor.

FORMULAS AND FACTS
- Deadlock-free process bound: R >= n(m-1)+1, so n_max = floor((R-1)/(m-1)) (R resources, each process needs m; e.g. R=12,m=4 gives 3)
- Banker: Need: Need = Max - Allocation; safe if some order lets every process finish with Available (In dec2019_q28 'Current needs' column is actually the allocation)
- Disk capacity: surfaces x tracks per surface x sectors per track x bytes per sector (Double-sided platters have 2 surfaces each)
- Sector-address bits: log2(surfaces x tracks x sectors) (Count total sectors, then bits)
- Rotational delay: max = 60/rpm seconds; average = half of that (5400 rpm gives 11.1 ms)
- Data transfer rate: bytes per track x revolutions per second (One track per revolution)
- Seek time: total head movement x time per cylinder (SSTF picks nearest pending request each time)
- Disk policies: SCAN goes to end then reverses; C-SCAN goes to end then jumps to start; LOOK/C-LOOK turn at the last request (C-SCAN return jump counted in textbook answers)
- Inode maximum file size: (direct + p + p^2) x block size, p = block size/address size (2KB blocks,4B addresses: p=512, about 513 MB)
- Tape write time: (data / recording density) / speed (+ inter-block gaps) (600000/1600/200 = 1.875 s)
- Paging sizes: pages = VA/page size; offset bits = log2(page); frames = PM/page; page table size = pages x entry size (Physical address bits = log2(PM size))
- Internal fragmentation: unused space in last page = pages x page size - process size (34 KB with 4 KB pages gives 2 KB)
- EMAT with TLB: h(t+m) + (1-h)(t+2m) (Single level page table; two-level adds extra m)
- EAT with page faults: (1-p)m + p x fault time; or p + q/100 if one fault per 100 (Hit ratio form h*t1 + (1-h)*t2)
- Swap time: 2 x (size/transfer rate) + latencies (15MB/30MBps=0.5s each way)
- Belady's anomaly: Occurs for FIFO; LRU and optimal are stack algorithms and have no anomaly (Common trap in statement questions)
- Little's law: n = lambda x W (20 = 10 x W gives 2 s)
- Scheduling times: TAT = CT - AT; WT = TAT - BT; RT = first run - AT; HRRN ratio = (W+S)/S (Weighted TAT = TAT/burst)
- RR worst-case wait: (n-1) x q (20 processes, q=4 gives 76 ms)
- Counting semaphore: final = initial - #P + #V (Solve for unknown #V)
- fork count: k sequential forks create 2^k processes (Count prints by tracing each fork)
- RAID levels: 0 striping,1 mirror,2 bit ECC,3 bit parity,4 block parity,5 distributed block parity,6 P+Q (Level 1 for write-heavy logs)
- Linux interrupt priority: user < kernel system service < bottom half < top half (Exact repeat)
- Thread sharing: Shared: code,data,files,address space. Private: stack,registers,PC (Threads of same process share address space)
- Thread model concurrency: one-to-one > many-to-many > many-to-one (Many-to-one blocks entirely on a blocking call)
- Boot order: ROM firmware -> boot block -> bootstrap loader -> kernel (Ordering trap)
- Layered file system: Application -> logical FS -> file organization module -> basic FS -> I/O control (Top to bottom)
- File allocation: Contiguous has external fragmentation; linked and indexed do not (Indexed supports direct+sequential access)
- Compiler phase order: lexical, syntax, semantic, intermediate code, optimization, code generation (Hash table best for symbol table)
- Unix facts: fork creates child; exec loads program; kill signals; clone selective sharing; wc -l; lpr; /etc/passwd; chmod -R a+x (Single-fact recall)

- Disk capacity / geometry arithmetic (5x): capacity = surfaces x tracks x sectors/track x bytes/sector; cylinders = tracks per surface; sector-address bits = log2(total sectors).

- Preemptive SJF / SRTF waiting or turnaround time (5x): Draw the Gantt chart; at every arrival compare remaining times. TAT = CT - AT; WT = TAT - BT.

- Mutual exclusion and critical-section statements (5x): Only one process in critical section; structure entry/critical/exit/remainder; spin lock = busy waiting; unaware processes still have mutual exclusion, starvation, deadlock problems but not coherence.
- Banker's algorithm passage (5x): Banker avoids deadlock; needs Max, Allocation, Available matrices/vectors; grants only if the system stays in a safe state.

- RAID level matching (4x): Memorise: 0 striping, 1 mirroring, 2 bit-level ECC (memory-style), 3 bit-interleaved parity, 4 block-interleaved parity, 5 block-interleaved distributed parity, 6 P+Q / Reed-Solomon.

- Match-the-following of OS terms (4x): Link each term to its area: Banker = resource allocation, demand paging = virtual memory, LFU = cache replacement, critical section = mutual exclusion, firmware = ROM, PCB = TCB, IPC = computational speedup.
- Non-preemptive FCFS / SJF / HRRN metrics on one process set (4x): FCFS by arrival; SJF picks the smallest burst among arrived processes; HRRN ratio = (W+S)/S. Weighted turnaround = TAT/burst.
- Scheduling theory statements (starvation, response time, quantum) (4x): SRTF and priority may starve; HRRN/aging fixes starvation; RR gives better response than FCFS; tiny quantum means many context switches.
- Thread concepts and models (4x): Threads share code, data and files but have own stack and registers; user library creates threads; concurrency one-to-one > many-to-many > many-to-one.
- Counting semaphore value after P and V operations (4x): final = initial - (#P) + (#V).
- Identify the 2nd request served / the policy from a head graph (3x): Trace the policy order on the same queue: C-LOOK(right) serves increasing requests then jumps to the lowest; SCAN(left) serves decreasing requests first. For a graph, look for a jump back without touching the disk end = C-LOOK.
- Virtual memory conceptual statements (3x): Virtual memory increases effective capacity; program can be larger than RAM; not all pages need to be loaded; address translation for every logical address.
- Process-creation system calls (fork, exec, clone, kill, exit) (3x): fork creates child; exec loads new program; kill sends signal; exit terminates; clone gives selective sharing flags (Linux).
- Round-robin waiting/turnaround and maximum wait (3x): Simulate the queue with quantum q; waiting = completion - arrival - burst; worst-case wait for n processes = (n-1)q.
- Rotational delay and data-transfer rate (2x): max rotational delay = 60/rpm s (avg = half); transfer rate = bytes per track x revolutions per second.
- File allocation methods and fragmentation (2x): Contiguous: external fragmentation, fast direct access. Linked: no external fragmentation, no direct access, pointer space. Indexed: direct + sequential, no external fragmentation, index-block overhead.
- Effective access time with TLB (2x): EMAT = h(t+m) + (1-h)(t+2m) for single-level paging (t = TLB time, m = memory time).
- Logical / virtual / physical address terminology (2x): Address in main memory = physical address; CPU-generated = logical (virtual); address space = logical/virtual set, memory space = physical set.
- Effective access time with page faults / hit ratio (2x): EAT = (1-p)*m + p*(fault service time); with hit ratio h: h*t_primary + (1-h)*t_secondary.
- Order of page-replacement steps (2x): Find page on disk; if no free frame use algorithm to pick victim, write it back if dirty, update tables; read in desired page; restart instruction.
- Linux interrupt protection level ordering (2x): Increasing priority: user mode < kernel system service routines < bottom half handlers < top half handlers.
- I/O protection and interrupts (2x): I/O instructions are privileged; with memory-mapped I/O protection is by the OS (memory protection); I/O completion interrupts are different from a trap for protection.
- Priority scheduling average waiting / response time (non-preemptive) (2x): Order by priority (lower number first), then cumulative start times give waiting times.
- Preemptive vs non-preemptive circumstances (2x): Preemption happens when running->ready or waiting->ready; non-preemptive SJF never context-switches mid-burst.
- OS-specific scheduling (Windows, Linux) (2x): Windows 16 non-real-time priorities (and 16 real-time); Linux supports preemptive priority and time-sharing.
- Maximum processes for deadlock freedom (2x): Deadlock-free if R >= n(m-1)+1, so n_max = floor((R-1)/(m-1)).
- Symbol table (2x): Symbol table used for storage allocation, type checking, duplicate-error suppression; hash table gives fastest access.
- Compiler phases order and roles (2x): Lexical -> syntax -> semantic -> intermediate code -> optimization -> code generation; syntax analysis checks grammar.

- DP steps: Characterize structure -> define recursively -> compute bottom-up -> construct solution (Only step 1 is shared with greedy.)
- FFT: Multiply degree-n polynomials in theta(n lg n); point-value product theta(n); Horner evaluation at n points theta(n^2) (Parallel FFT span theta(lg n).)
- Full m-ary tree: L=(m-1)*I+1; total nodes = m*I+1 (41 leaves, 10 internal -> m=5.)

- Radix sort cost: d digits, radix k: theta(d(n+k)); integers in 0..n^2-1 sort in O(n) (9*5*8=360.)
- Second smallest: n + ceil(lg n) - 2 comparisons (tournament) (Worst case.)
- NP facts: NPC in P => P=NP; NPC = NP intersect NP-hard; P subset of co-NP; NP != co-NP => P != NP; vertex cover 2-approx; TSP triangle-inequality 2-approx (EXP = 2^(n^k), not 2^k.)

- Decidability: Rice theorem and TM undecidable problems (4x): Any non-trivial property of L(M) is undecidable (equivalence, emptiness, finiteness, regularity). Halting is undecidable. Properties of the machine code itself or bounded simulation are decidable.

- PDA language from transitions (3x): Trace stack effect: pushes per a, pops per b gives ratio language (push 3 pop 1 gives a^n b^3n; 11 per a gives a^2n b^n). Start-state epsilon move to final adds the empty string (n≥0 vs n>0).

- CFG simplification and decision on CFL (reduced grammar, order, finiteness) (3x): Order: remove epsilon, then unit, then useless (non-generating before unreachable). Finiteness of CFL decided on non-redundant CNF grammar of L-{Λ} by looking for a cycle.

- Regex containment and equivalence (3x): Rewrite each regex as a description set; (a*+b)*=(a+b)*; s=aa*b ⊂ a*b; a(a+b)+ ⊂ a(a+b)*. Check inclusion by sample strings.

- Code optimisation concepts (3x): Constant folding = compile-time evaluation; loops identified by dominators, depth-first order, reducible graphs.

- LL(1)/FOLLOW computation (2x): FOLLOW(X) = FIRST of what comes after X; if nullable add FOLLOW of the parent. LL(1) requires unambiguous grammar with no left recursion and disjoint FIRST.

FORMULAS AND FACTS
- Transmission delay: Tt = frame size (bits) / bandwidth (bps) (Convert bytes to bits first.)

- Bandwidth-delay product: BDP = bandwidth x delay (RTT if round trip given) (Result in bits.)
- Optimal sliding-window size: W = 1 + 2Tp/Tt (Sequence bits n: window <= 2^n - 1 (go-back-N) or 2^(n-1) (SR).)

- Hamming distance: Number of bit positions where two words differ (weight of XOR) (Decode to nearest valid codeword.)
- CRC codeword: Codeword = dataword || remainder (remainder from modulo-2 division after appending zeros) ((x+1) factor of G(x) catches all odd-bit errors (nov2021_q100).)
- Bit stuffing flag: Frame flag 01111110 = 0x7E; stuff 0 after five consecutive 1s (Flag is hex 7E.)
- Nyquist bit rate: C = 2B log2(L) (Noiseless channel only; sampling rate >= 2 f_max.)
- Shannon capacity: C = B log2(1 + SNR) (Noisy channel; SNR is a ratio, not dB.)
- Frequency and period: f = 1/T (100 ms = 10 Hz = 10^-2 kHz.)
- Fully connected links: n(n-1)/2 (Symmetric keys for N persons also N(N-1)/2 (dec2018_q90).)
- CSMA/CD minimum frame: L_min = bandwidth x 2Tp (Round-trip time, not one way.)
- Slotted ALOHA throughput: S = G e^(-G); pure ALOHA S = G e^(-2G) (G = frames per frame time.)
- Token bucket burst duration: T = C / (M - rho) = capacity / (output rate - token rate) (16/(10-2) = 2 s.)
- Token ring 1-bit delay: distance per bit = propagation speed / bit rate (200 m/us / 10 Mbps = 20 m.)
- Hosts per subnet: 2^(host bits) - 2; subnets = 2^(subnet bits) (Subtract 2 for network and broadcast addresses.)
- Subnetting a block: new prefix = old prefix + log2(subnets); addresses = 2^(32 - prefix) (1024 subnets from /16 gives /26 and 64 addresses.)
- IPv4 class ranges: A 0-127, B 128-191, C 192-223, D 224-239, E 240-255; A=50%, B=25%, C=12.5% of space (127.x.x.x loopback is class A.)
- IP fragmentation: data per fragment = floor((MTU - 20)/8)*8; offset = bytes/8 (MTU 820 gives 800 data bytes.)
- IPv4 header decode: byte0 low nibble HLEN x 4; bytes 2-3 total length; byte 8 TTL; byte 9 protocol (6 TCP, 17 UDP, 1 ICMP) (Efficiency = (total - header)/total.)
- RSA: n = pq; phi = (p-1)(q-1); ed = 1 mod phi; C = M^e mod n; M = C^d mod n (Private-key encryption gives digital signature.)
- Symmetric key count: N(N-1)/2 keys for N parties (Public-key needs only N key pairs.)
- Cipher sizes: DES 64-bit block/56-bit key; 3DES 168; AES 128 block, 128/192/256 key; IDEA 64/128; Blowfish 32-448 (DES has 16 rounds; function steps: expansion, XOR key, S-box, P-box.)
- Line coding average bandwidth: NRZ-L N/2; MLT-3 N/3; 2B1Q N/4; 4D-PAM5 N/8; Manchester bit rate = half baud (Manchester needs twice the bandwidth of NRZ.)
- DHCP sequence: Discover, Offer, Request, Ack (Renewal: timer, request, ack.)
- Hierarchical routing table size: entries = routers in own region + other regions in cluster + other clusters (Key gives 25 for the 720-router example.)

- Fuzzy complement: mu_A'(x)=1-mu_A(x) (Apply per element.)
- Fuzzy intersection / union: min(muA,muB) / max(muA,muB) (Standard Zadeh operators.)
- Algebraic sum / bounded sum / bounded difference: a+b-ab ; min(1,a+b) ; max(0,a-b) (Bounded sum uses min with 1.)
- Dual t-norm and s-norm: t(x,y)=1-s(1-x,1-y) (Substitute then simplify.)
- alpha-cut nesting: alpha1<alpha2 => A_alpha1 contains A_alpha2 (Higher cut gives smaller set.)
- Crossover point: mu_A(x)=0.5 (Core is mu=1, support is mu>0.)
- Number of models: 2^n assignments over n symbols; models of OR = 2^n - falsifying (B v C over 4 symbols gives 12; 4-literal clause gives 15.)
- Entailment: alpha |= beta iff M(alpha) subset of M(beta) (False |= anything.)
- Existential translation: exists x (P(x) AND Q(x)) (Never use implication with exists.)
- Minimax / alpha-beta: MAX takes max, MIN takes min; alpha=-inf, beta=+inf initially; best case O(b^(d/2)) (Alpha-beta gives same value as minimax.)
- A* evaluation: f(n)=g(n)+h(n); admissible: h<=h* (Consistent: h(n)<=c(n,n')+h(n').)
- Search complexities: BFS O(b^d); DFS O(bm); DLS O(bl); IDS O(bd) (Space complexity; RBFS is O(bd) space.)
- GA selection probability: p(x)=f(x)/sum f(x) (Convert binary chromosome first.)

- Certainty factors: AND: min; OR: max; CF(conclusion)=CF(premise)*CF(rule) (Example: min(0.5,0.8)=0.5 times 0.8 = 0.40.)
- Dempster-Shafer: Bel(A)+Bel(not A) <= 1 (Not equal 1 unlike probability.)
- Sigmoid: f(x)=1/(1+e^-x); f'=f(1-f); for 1/(1+e^-2x), f'(0)=2*0.25=0.5 (Scaling factor 2 doubles derivative.)
- Neuron weighted sum: y=k*sum w_i x_i (1*5+2*7+3*10+4*30=169, times 3 = 507.)
- Perceptron rule: w_new=w+eta*(t-y)*x (Single layer separates AND, OR, NOR but not XOR.)
- Gradient descent update: W(t+1)=W(t)-alpha*dE/dW (Minus sign.)
- Kohonen SOM update: w_new=(1-eta)*w_old+eta*x (Winner and neighbours.)
- K-means / Manhattan distance: centroid=mean of cluster points; d=|x1-x2|+|y1-y2| (Recompute centroid after assignment.)
- Decision tree to rules: AND along a branch, OR across branches (Disjunctive normal form.)
- Environment property: uncertain = not fully observable OR not deterministic; semi-dynamic: environment static but score changes (Common trap.)

QUESTION FAMILIES (most repeated first; each is a question type the exam keeps reusing)
- Agent types, architecture and environments (7x): Simple reflex agent uses only current percept; utility-based handles happy/unhappy; learning agent improves performance; environment properties: observable, deterministic, static, semi-dynamic (environment fixed, performance score changes), uncertain = not fully observable OR not deterministic. MAS: multiple agents with diverse objectives and communication.
- A* optimality and heuristic admissibility (6x): A* optimal with admissible h (tree) / consistent h (graph); admissible = never overestimates; consistent = triangle inequality; A* expands all nodes with f<C* and none with f>C*; max of admissible heuristics dominates.
- GA odd-one-out: operators, encodings, selection (5x): Mutation: random resetting, scramble, inversion, swap, bit flip. Representations: binary, real, permutation (Gray also). Parent selection: roulette/fitness-proportional, tournament, rank, Boltzmann. 'Actual count' relates to selection.
- Backpropagation and weight update (5x): Backprop propagates error backward from output to input; gradient descent: W(t+1)=W(t)-alpha dE/dW. Training order: initialize weights, feed forward, loss, backprop, update.
- ANN passage questions (June 2024 re-exam) (5x): Read the passage: ANNs are inspired by the brain; input/hidden/output layers; weights adjusted to reduce error.
- Minimax root value of a game tree (4x): Evaluate bottom-up: MAX nodes take max of children, MIN nodes take min. Alpha-beta gives the same root value.
- Alpha-beta pruning true/false statements (4x): Facts: minimax is depth-first; alpha-beta returns the same value as minimax; pruning efficiency depends on move ordering; alpha init -inf, beta +inf; values updated along the search path; best case halves depth (O(b^(d/2))).
- Supervised vs unsupervised vs classification algorithm identification (4x): Supervised: regression, KNN, decision tree, logistic regression, SVM, backprop. Unsupervised: clustering, PCA, Apriori, SOM. Reinforcement: reward/punish with MDP. Regression is not classification.
- Clustering algorithm steps and k-means calculation (4x): K-means: choose k, init centroids, assign to nearest, update centroids as mean, repeat. DBSCAN: eps neighbours, core points via MinPts, expand density-connected points. Compute distance (Manhattan = sum |dx|+|dy|) to a recomputed centroid.
- Planning and STRIPS (4x): STRIPS is action-centric: each action has precondition and effect (add/delete lists); features are primitive or derived; no conditional effects directly. Planning graph gives heuristics; relaxation drops negative effects. Classic planning definition: init, actions, goal.
- ANN features and layer statements (4x): ANN: machine learning algorithm, handles large data, extracts features automatically, modelled on brain; training time grows with size; can be simulated on conventional computer; can include feedback. Information flows input, hidden, output.
- NN numerical computation (4x): Neuron output = f(sum w_i x_i + bias); linear transfer multiplies by constant; sigmoid 1/(1+e^-x), derivative f(1-f); perceptron update w += eta (t - y) x.
- Fuzzy set operations on membership values (3x): Complement=1-mu; intersection=min; union=max; algebraic sum=a+b-ab; bounded sum=min(1,a+b); bounded difference=max(0,a-b). Apply element-wise.
- Entailment definition and properties (3x): alpha entails beta (alpha |= beta) iff beta true in every model where alpha true; False entails everything; alpha |= (b and g) implies alpha |= b and alpha |= g; Horn KB works with forward/backward chaining.
- NLP components and NLU vs NLG (3x): NLU: morphological, syntactic, semantic, pragmatic analysis (no 'meaning analysis'). NLG: text planning, sentence planning, realization. Parsing: top-down, bottom-up, dependency, Earley; SMT is not a parser.
- Match search algorithms to evaluation function / space complexity (3x): Greedy: h(n); UCS/lowest-cost: g(n); A*: g+h. Space: BFS O(b^d), DFS O(bm), DLS O(bl), IDS O(bd).
- Dual pair of fuzzy t-norm and s-norm (2x): Use t(x,y)=1-s(1-x,1-y), so s(x,y)=1-t(1-x,1-y). Substitute 1-x,1-y into t, simplify 1 - (1-x)(1-y)/((1-x)+(1-y)-(1-x)(1-y)).
- Alpha-cut properties (2x): Alpha-cut = elements with mu>=alpha. Higher alpha gives smaller set (nested, decreasing). Union/intersection commute with cuts; complement does not except special cases.
- Count models of a propositional sentence (2x): Models over n symbols = 2^n assignments; count assignments making the sentence true. For an OR of literals, 2^n minus falsifying assignments.
- English to FOL: 'a country that borders both ...' (2x): Existential quantifier pairs with conjunction (AND), never implication.
- Knowledge-base design steps order (2x): Order: choose task domain, select atoms for propositions, axiomatize the domain, ask questions about the intended interpretation.
- GA fitness and selection probability calculation (2x): Fitness f(x); selection probability = f(x)/sum f; the parent chosen is the one with highest fitness. Convert binary string to decimal before f(x)=x^2.
- GA step sequence (2x): Order: initialization/evaluate fitness, selection of parents, crossover (prob pc), mutation (prob pm), repeat until termination.
